Definition: from G5574; untrue, i.e. erroneous, deceitful, wicked:--false, liar.
BiblicalUsage: Pseudes means false, untrue, deceitful. The council set up false witnesses against Stephen, who said the man ceaseth not to speak blasphemous words against the holy place. Christ commends Ephesus, because thou hast tried them which say they are apostles, and are not, and hast found them liars. And in the last judgment, all liars shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe falsehood is never harmless: false witnesses killed Stephen, false apostles troubled Ephesus, and liars are shut out of the city at the end. I hold that truth is worth trying every claim against, because the liar's end is the lake of fire.
